purpose: Paired, query-matched comparison of the study's corrected rejected-cell SAC count against sample-adapted SAC-Basic/Row/Column histogram tests
adaptation: Published tests use 2^20 inputs, eight bins and alpha 0.01. This follow-up uses exact Bin(N,1/2) quantile bins at smaller N and a primary alpha of 0.001. It is not a full numerical replication of the published cipher experiments. No upstream implementation is copied.
sample_design: Nested prefixes within a replicate; new independent pseudorandom input sequence for each replicate. All methods use the same full SAC count matrix, requiring N(n+1) trace inputs. Query budgets are matched within each cipher, not across state widths.
rng: NumPy PCG64; SeedSequence([base_seed, stage_id, state_bits, sample_size_or_replicate])
histogram_bins: Eight contiguous count bins; cuts at Bin(N,1/2) first integer CDF >= j/8 for j=1..7, inclusive upper boundary. Exact unequal discrete bin masses are retained. Pearson df=7; minimum row-bin expected count exceeds five for specified designs.
nominal_policy: Corrected SAC count uses its exact Bin(n^2,q_N) upper tail. Basic uses chi-square sf(7 df); Row/Column use Sidak aggregation of the smallest row/column chi-square p-value, following the paper's rule. Add the same finite-domain coupling bound to all family p-values.
primary_policy: Corrected SAC count retains exact tail. Basic and maximum row/column Pearson statistics use plus-one Monte Carlo rank p-values against 100000 independent calibration matrices, including ties. Row and column maxima have the same ideal-label marginal null law. Add the same finite-domain bound. These are MC-calibrated variants of the histogram tests, explicitly distinct from the published asymptotic rules.
null_model: Independent uniform output labels on disjoint input stars; count cells are iid Bin(N,1/2). Simulate row multinomial bin histograms as sufficient statistics for Basic and maximum-axis tests. Simulate rejected-cell counts from their exact binomial null. These draws evaluate marginal null sizes, not joint cross-detector behavior or full cipher/permutation executions.
finite_domain_bound: delta_A = min(1,[N(n+1)]^2/2^n), covering input-star overlaps and random-function/permutation switching under the ideal-permutation reference
reporting: Per-condition rejection frequencies and Wilson 95% intervals; paired discordant outcomes and exact McNemar tests; Holm correction over 90 baseline-vs-comparator contrasts for primary MC-calibrated alpha=0.001 analysis. Other policy/alpha families are labeled sensitivity analyses. No hypothesis treats serial rounds or nested samples as independent observations.
limitations: Conditional on two fixed default keys and chosen round windows. Does not estimate behavior over all keys or establish cipher security, universal superiority, or equivalence from a nonsignificant difference. Null calibration is checked on held-out simulation with finite uncertainty; nominal alpha is a ceiling, not identical realized size across discrete tests. No SAC-2 or neural comparison is included.
